# Core Architecture and Design Philosophy



BioSimSpace embodies a unified, engine-agnostic framework for biomolecular simulation workflows. The architecture prioritizes interoperability, type safety, and workflow composability through a layered design that abstracts backend simulation engines while providing rich functionality for molecular modeling, simulation protocols, and process management.

## Architectural Overview

BioSimSpace follows a modular, layered architecture that separates concerns between molecular representation, simulation protocols, execution engines, and workflow interfaces. The design centers on creating a consistent user experience across multiple simulation backends while maintaining engine-specific capabilities.

![BioSimSpace Architecture](https://github.com/OpenBioSim/biosimspace/blob/devel/paper/figures/fig2.png?raw=true)

The architecture can be conceptualized as three primary layers with supporting infrastructure:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Workflow Layer"
        GW["Gateway - Multi-interface Node System"]
        NB["Notebook - Interactive Visualization"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Simulation Layer"
        PROT["Protocol - Simulation Protocols"]
        PROC["Process - Engine Execution"]
        FE["FreeEnergy - FEP/ATM Calculations"]
        META["Metadynamics - Enhanced Sampling"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Molecular Layer"
        SYS["System - Molecular System Container"]
        MOL["Molecule - Molecular Entity Wrapper"]
        SIRE["_SireWrappers - Sire Object Abstraction"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Infrastructure Layer"
        TYPES["Types - Type-safe Physical Quantities"]
        UNITS["Units - Unit Conversion System"]
        CONVERT["Convert - Format Interoperability"]
        STREAM["Stream - Serialization"]
        IO["IO - File I/O Operations"]
    end
    
    GW --> PROT
    NB --> SYS
    PROT --> PROC
    PROC --> SYS
    PROC --> FE
    PROC --> META
    FE --> SYS
    META --> SYS
    SYS --> SIRE
    SIRE --> TYPES
    CONVERT --> IO
    STREAM --> IO
```

## Core Design Principles

### Engine Agnosticism

BioSimSpace's foundational principle is providing a consistent API across multiple molecular dynamics engines. This is achieved through abstract base classes that define common interfaces, with engine-specific implementations inheriting from these bases. The `Process` class serves as the primary abstraction for simulation execution [python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L50-L51](python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L50-L51).

The architecture supports five primary engines through specialized process implementations:
- **AMBER**: Native AMBER MD simulations
- **GROMACS**: GROMACS-based simulations
- **NAMD**: NAMD molecular dynamics
- **OpenMM**: OpenMM-accelerated simulations
- **SOMD**: Sire OpenMD implementation

Each engine-specific process (e.g., `_amber.py`, `_gromacs.py`) inherits from the base `Process` class, implementing engine-specific command generation, configuration file handling, and output parsing while maintaining a unified user interface.

### Type Safety and Physical Units

BioSimSpace enforces type safety through a comprehensive physical type system that prevents unit errors and enables automatic conversion. All physical quantities are expressed as typed objects with associated units rather than raw numbers. The `Type` base class provides the foundation for all physical quantities [python/BioSimSpace/Types/_type.py#L30-L31](python/BioSimSpace/Types/_type.py#L30-L31).

The type system implements:
- **Dimensional analysis**: Each type tracks dimensions (mass, length, time, temperature, charge, angle)
- **Operator overloading**: Arithmetic operations preserve type information and perform unit conversions
- **Automatic conversion**: The `to()` method enables seamless unit conversion with dimensional consistency checking
- **String parsing**: Types can be instantiated from string representations

| Physical Dimension | Type Classes | Example Units |
|-------------------|--------------|---------------|
| Length | `Length` | Angstrom, nanometer, picometer |
| Energy | `Energy` | kcal/mol, kJ/mol, hartree |
| Time | `Time` | femtosecond, picosecond, nanosecond |
| Temperature | `Temperature` | Kelvin, Celsius |
| Pressure | `Pressure` | bar, atm, atmosphere |
| Angle | `Angle` | degree, radian |

> [!TIP]
> All physical quantities in BioSimSpace should be created using typed constructors rather than raw numbers. This ensures dimensional consistency and enables automatic validation. For example, use `BSS.Types.Temperature(300, "kelvin")` instead of `300.0` to represent temperature values.

### Protocol-Based Simulation Design

Simulation protocols in BioSimSpace are defined as declarative specifications rather than imperative procedures. The `Protocol` class hierarchy provides a structured way to define simulation parameters while allowing for customization [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_protocol.py#L31-L40](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_protocol.py#L31-L40).

Protocol types include:
- **Minimisation**: Energy minimization protocols
- **Equilibration**: System equilibration protocols
- **Production**: Production MD simulation protocols
- **FreeEnergy**: Free energy calculation protocols with mixin support
- **Metadynamics**: Enhanced sampling protocol configuration
- **Custom**: User-defined protocol specifications

Protocols implement mixins for cross-cutting concerns:
- `_PositionRestraintMixin`: Adds position restraint functionality
- `_FreeEnergyMixin`: Provides free energy simulation parameters
- Protocol inheritance enables composition of specialized behaviors

This design enables reproducible simulations through protocol serialization and validation, separating simulation intent from execution details.

## Molecular System Abstraction

### Sire Wrapper Architecture

BioSimSpace wraps the Sire molecular simulation library to provide a higher-level, more user-friendly interface. The `_SireWrappers` module contains thin wrappers around Sire objects that present a Pythonic API while preserving the full power of the underlying molecular representation [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L22-L24](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L22-L24).

The `System` class serves as the primary container for molecular systems, providing:

- **Molecule management**: Add, remove, update, and query molecules
- **Selection and querying**: Search for molecules, residues, atoms based on criteria
- **Geometric operations**: Translation, rotation, box manipulation
- **Property access**: Charges, coordinates, topological information
- **Perturbation support**: Handle perturbable molecules for free energy calculations

The wrapper design pattern provides several advantages:
- **Simplified API**: More intuitive method names and signatures
- **Error handling**: Pythonic exceptions rather than C++ style errors
- **Operator overloading**: Natural syntax for system operations
- **Index management**: Transparent handling of molecule and atom indexing

### System Composition and Manipulation

BioSimSpace Systems support rich composition patterns through operator overloading. The `__add__` and `__sub__` operators enable natural system merging and subtraction operations [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L153-L167](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L153-L167).

```python
# Merge two systems
combined = system1 + system2

# Remove molecules from a system
reduced = system1 - ligand_molecule
```

The System class implements container protocol methods (`__contains__`, `__getitem__`, `__iter__`, `__len__`) to support Pythonic iteration and access patterns. Molecules can be accessed by index or queried using sophisticated search criteria.

### Serialization and Streaming

Large molecular systems require efficient serialization for workflow components and checkpointing. The `Stream` module provides functionality for saving and loading Sire objects with metadata preservation [python/BioSimSpace/Stream/_stream.py#L32-L84](python/BioSimSpace/Stream/_stream.py#L32-L84).

The streaming implementation:
- **Compresses** molecular data to reduce storage requirements
- **Preserves** metadata for provenance tracking
- **Enables** incremental loading of large systems
- **Supports** cross-platform serialization

## Process Management Architecture

### Abstract Process Base Class

The `Process` class provides the foundation for all simulation execution, defining a consistent interface across engines while allowing engine-specific customization [python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L53-L65](python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L53-L65).

Key Process capabilities include:
- **Lifecycle management**: Start, stop, wait, kill operations
- **Configuration**: Get, set, and modify simulation parameters
- **Monitoring**: Check status, view output, collect data
- **Input/output management**: Access input files, retrieve trajectories
- **Argument manipulation**: Modify command-line arguments flexibly

### Multi-Engine Execution Model

Process subclasses implement engine-specific execution logic through template methods:
- `_generate_args()`: Generate command-line arguments [python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L1665-L1666](python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L1665-L1666)
- Configuration file generation and parsing
- Output file parsing and data extraction
- Engine-specific validation and error handling

The Process architecture enables:
- **Engine swapping**: Change engines without modifying workflow logic
- **Reproducibility**: Consistent protocol execution across engines
- **Resource management**: Efficient handling of computational resources
- **Error detection**: Engine-specific error detection and reporting

### Real-Time Data Streaming

BioSimSpace processes support real-time data collection through streaming interfaces. Processes can continuously monitor output files and provide access to time series data without waiting for completion [python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L420-L494](python/BioSimSpace/Process/_process.py#L420-L494).

Data collection methods include:
- `_getTime()`: Extract simulation time series
- `_getCollectiveVariable()`: Monitor collective variables
- `_getFreeEnergy()`: Track free energy estimates
- `_sampleConfigurations()`: Sample system configurations

## Gateway Workflow System

### Multi-Interface Node Architecture

The Gateway module provides a sophisticated workflow node system that generates multiple interfaces from a single definition. The `Node` class serves as the central abstraction for creating reusable workflow components [python/BioSimSpace/Gateway/_node.py#L246-L247](python/BioSimSpace/Gateway/_node.py#L246-L247).

Gateway nodes automatically generate interfaces for:
- **Command-line interfaces (CLI)**: argparse-based command parsing
- **Jupyter notebooks**: Interactive widgets for parameter input
- **KNIME nodes**: Integration with KNIME analytics platform
- **Common Workflow Language (CWL)**: Portable workflow specifications

### Input/Output Abstraction

Gateway uses typed input requirements with validation, documentation, and default values. Each input specification generates appropriate UI elements and validation logic for all supported interfaces [python/BioSimSpace/Gateway/_node.py#L415-L460](python/BioSimSpace/Gateway/_node.py#L415-L460).

Input types include:
- **Simple types**: Boolean, integer, float, string
- **File types**: Single file, file set with format validation
- **Physical quantities**: Typed values with units
- **Composite types**: Lists, tuples with element validation

The output system allows nodes to publish results with automatic type inference and interface generation. Output values can be files, text data, or molecular systems.

### Metadata and Provenance

Gateway nodes capture comprehensive metadata for reproducibility:
- **Author information**: Name, email, affiliation
- **Documentation**: Description, help text, examples
- **Versioning**: License information and version tracking
- **Validation**: Input validation and error messages

## Interoperability and Conversion

### Format Conversion Layer

BioSimSpace provides extensive format conversion capabilities through the `Convert` module, supporting bidirectional conversion between BioSimSpace, Sire, OpenMM, RDKit, and various file formats [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L137-L463](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L137-L463).

The conversion system handles:
- **Structure formats**: PDB, MOL2, SDF, GRO, PRMTOP, PSF
- **Coordinate formats**: CRD, RST7, TRR, XTC
- **Trajectory formats**: DCD, NC, TRJ
- **Molecule representations**: SMILES, SMARTS

The `to()` function provides automatic format detection and conversion based on file extensions or explicit format specification.

### OpenMM Integration

BioSimSpace provides native OpenMM integration through dedicated conversion routines [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L487-L556](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L487-L556). This enables:
- **Direct OpenMM execution**: Use BioSimSpace protocols with OpenMM
- **System conversion**: Convert BioSimSpace systems to OpenMM objects
- **Force field mapping**: Preserve force field parameters during conversion
- **Custom forces**: Maintain custom force definitions

## Error Handling and Validation

### Exception Hierarchy

BioSimSpace defines a comprehensive exception hierarchy for error handling [python/BioSimSpace/_Exceptions/_exceptions.py](python/BioSimSpace/_Exceptions/_exceptions.py). The exception system provides:
- **Type-specific exceptions**: Type errors, value errors, file errors
- **Informative messages**: Clear error descriptions with context
- **Recovery guidance**: Suggestions for fixing errors
- **Verbose mode**: Optional detailed error information

The main module includes verbosity control that can be set before import to enable detailed error messages during initialization.

### Input Validation

Gateway nodes and Process implementations perform comprehensive input validation:
- **Type checking**: Verify input types match specifications
- **Range validation**: Check numeric values within acceptable ranges
- **File existence**: Validate input files exist and are readable
- **Unit consistency**: Ensure physical quantities have compatible units

> [!TIP]
> Enable verbose error messages during development by setting the environment variable `BSS_VERBOSE_ERRORS=1` before importing BioSimSpace. This provides detailed stack traces and context information that aids debugging.

## Configuration and Environment

### Environment Detection

BioSimSpace automatically detects the execution environment and adjusts behavior accordingly [python/BioSimSpace/__init__.py#L34-L67](python/BioSimSpace/__init__.py#L34-L67). The system detects:
- **Jupyter notebooks**: Enables interactive widgets and rich output
- **Terminal interaction**: Adjusts output formatting and error messages
- **Engine availability**: Checks for installed simulation packages

### Engine Configuration

The `_Config` module manages engine-specific configuration [python/BioSimSpace/_Config/_config.py](python/BioSimSpace/_Config/_config.py). Configuration includes:
- **Executable location**: Find simulation engine executables
- **Version detection**: Determine engine versions and capabilities
- **Environment setup**: Configure environment variables and paths

## Design Philosophy Summary

BioSimSpace's architecture embodies several key philosophical principles:

1. **Abstraction without loss of control**: Provide simple interfaces while maintaining access to low-level capabilities when needed
2. **Reproducibility by design**: Protocols, validation, and serialization support reproducible workflows
3. **Interoperability first**: Support multiple engines and formats through unified interfaces
4. **Type safety**: Catch errors at development time through typed physical quantities
5. **Workflow composability**: Enable creation of complex workflows from simple components
6. **Extensibility**: Allow users to extend functionality through custom protocols, nodes, and types

This architecture enables researchers to focus on scientific questions rather than implementation details, while maintaining the flexibility needed for advanced computational studies.

# Supported File Formats and Conversion



BioSimSpace provides comprehensive support for reading and writing molecular simulation file formats, enabling seamless workflow integration across different computational chemistry tools. This documentation covers the complete format ecosystem and conversion capabilities available in BioSimSpace.

## Format Ecosystem Architecture

BioSimSpace's file format support is built on top of the Sire molecular simulation framework, providing a unified interface for handling molecular data across multiple simulation packages. The system consists of three interconnected modules:

- **IO Module**: Core read/write operations for molecular systems
- **Convert Module**: Format conversion between different representations (BioSimSpace, Sire, RDKit, OpenMM)
- **File Cache**: Optional caching system for performance optimization

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Sources"
        A[Local Files]
        B[URLs/Remote]
        C[PDB Database]
        D[Directory Wildcards]
    end
    
    subgraph "IO Layer"
        E[readMolecules]
        F[readPDB]
        G[readPerturbableSystem]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Processing"
        H[Sire MoleculeParser]
        I[Format Detection]
        J[Property Mapping]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conversion Layer"
        K[BioSimSpace Objects]
        L[Sire Objects]
        M[RDKit Objects]
        N[OpenMM Objects]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Formats"
        O[AMBER<br/>prm7/rst7]
        P[GROMACS<br/>gro/top]
        Q[PDB]
        R[SDF]
        S[Other Formats]
    end
    
    A --> E
    B --> E
    C --> F
    D --> E
    G -->|Perturbable Molecules| H
    
    E --> I
    F --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    
    K <--> L
    K <--> M
    K <--> N
    
    K --> O
    K --> P
    K --> Q
    K --> R
    K --> S
    
    style H fill:#f9f,stroke:#333
    style K fill:#bbf,stroke:#333
```

## Supported File Formats

BioSimSpace automatically detects and processes a wide variety of molecular file formats. The format information is captured from the underlying Sire framework's `MoleculeParser.supported_formats()` [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L60-L80).

### Format Categories and Capabilities

The supported formats span multiple simulation packages and use cases:

| Format | Extension(s) | Read | Write | Description | Notes |
|--------|-------------|------|-------|-------------|-------|
| **AMBER** | prm7, rst7, crd, top | ✓ | ✓ | AMBER topology and coordinate files | Supports velocity information; geometric combining rules warnings |
| **GROMACS** | gro87, grotop, top, gro | ✓ | ✓ | GROMACS coordinate and topology files | Requires GROMACS installation for topology support; water topology matching available |
| **PDB** | pdb | ✓ | ✓ | Protein Data Bank format | Direct PDB ID support; optional pdb4amber processing |
| **SDF** | sdf | ✓ | ✓ | Structure-Data File format | Preserves stereochemistry; supports multiple molecules |
| **MOL2** | mol2 | ✓ | ✓ | Tripos mol2 format | |
| **PSF** | psf | ✓ | ✓ | CHARMM/X-PLOR PSF | NAMD compatibility |
| **XYZ** | xyz | ✓ | ✓ | Cartesian coordinate format | |
| **DL-POLY** | config | ✓ | ✓ | DL-POLY format | |
| **LAMMPS** | lammpsdata | ✓ | ✓ | LAMMPS data file | |
| **OpenMM** | xml | ✓ | ✓ | OpenMM XML format | Via Convert module |
| **Perturbable** | - | ✓ | ✓ | Dual-end state for FEP | AMBER format with end state files |

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L60-L80), [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L800-L900)

### Format Information Access

Query detailed information about any supported format programmatically:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Get all supported formats
formats = BSS.IO.fileFormats()
print(f"Supported formats: {formats}")

# Get detailed information about a specific format
info = BSS.IO.formatInfo("PDB")
print(f"PDB format info: {info}")
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L130-L150)

## Reading Molecular Systems

### Basic File Reading

The `readMolecules()` function is the primary interface for loading molecular systems from files. It automatically handles format detection, URL downloads, and wildcard expansion:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Read from local files
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["ala.rst7", "ala.prm7"])

# Read from URLs (automatic download)
files = BSS.IO.expand(
    BSS.tutorialUrl(),
    ["ala.crd", "ala.top"],
    ".bz2"
)
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(files)

# Read all files in a directory
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules("dir/*")
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L318-L399)

### Advanced Reading Options

The `readMolecules()` function provides several parameters for controlling the reading process:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `files` | str, [str] | required | File path(s) or URLs |
| `make_whole` | bool | False | Unwrap molecules across periodic boundaries |
| `rotate_box` | bool | False | Rotate box vectors for MD engine compatibility |
| `reduce_box` | bool | False | Reduce box vectors to minimum size |
| `show_warnings` | bool | False | Display parsing warnings |
| `download_dir` | str | None | Directory for downloaded files |
| `property_map` | dict | {} | Custom property name mapping |

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L318-L400)

### Custom Property Mapping

Map system properties to custom names for interoperability with different tools:

```python
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(
    ["ala.rst7", "ala.prm7"],
    property_map={"charge": "my-charge"}
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L318-L400)

### GROMACS Topology Support

When reading GROMACS files, you can specify a custom GROMACS topology directory:

```python
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(
    ["mol.gro87", "mol.grotop"],
    property_map={"GROMACS_PATH": "/path/to/gromacs/topology"}
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L450-L470)

### Specialized PDB Reading

The `readPDB()` function provides direct access to PDB structures with AMBER-specific processing:

```python
# Read by PDB ID (downloads from RCSB)
system = BSS.IO.readPDB("1a3n")

# Read from file with pdb4amber preprocessing
system = BSS.IO.readPDB("file.pdb", pdb4amber=True)

# Control processing options
system = BSS.IO.readPDB(
    "1a3n",
    pdb4amber=True,
    work_dir="/tmp/pdb_processing",
    show_warnings=True
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L220-L318)

### Perturbable System Reading

For free energy calculations, read systems with dual-end state representations:

```python
perturbable_system = BSS.IO.readPerturbableSystem(
    top0="perturbable_system0.prm7",
    coords0="perturbable_system0.rst7",
    top1="perturbable_system1.prm7",
    coords1="perturbable_system1.rst7"
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L920-L1000), [tests/IO/test_perturbable.py](tests/IO/test_perturbable.py#L1-L28)

## Writing Molecular Systems

### Basic File Writing

Save molecular systems to various formats using `saveMolecules()`:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Load a system
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["ala.rst7", "ala.prm7"])

# Save to a different format
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, "pdb")

# Save to multiple formats
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, ["gro87", "grotop"])
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L600-L900)

### Writing Options

The `saveMolecules()` function provides parameters for controlling output:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `filebase` | str | required | Base name for output files |
| `system` | System/Molecule | required | Molecular system to save |
| `fileformat` | str, [str] | required | Target format(s) |
| `match_water` | bool | True | Update water naming for target format |
| `save_velocities` | bool | True | Write velocity information |
| `property_map` | dict | {} | Custom property name mapping |

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L600-L700)

### Water Topology Matching

When converting between AMBER and GROMACS formats, water molecule naming conventions differ. The `match_water` parameter automatically handles this:

```python
# Convert AMBER to GROMACS with water topology adjustment
BSS.IO.saveMolecules(
    "gromacs_system",
    amber_system,
    ["gro87", "grotop"],
    match_water=True
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L800-L900)

### Force Field Considerations

AMBER topology files cannot represent force fields using geometric combining rules. BioSimSpace warns users when writing such systems:

```python
# Warning: Geometric combining rules will be lost on read
system_with_geo_rules = load_system_with_geometric_rules()
BSS.IO.saveMolecules("amber", system_with_geo_rules, "prm7")
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L800-L850)

### Perturbable System Writing

Save free energy perturbation systems with dual-end state files:

```python
BSS.IO.savePerturbableSystem(
    filebase="perturbable",
    system=perturbable_system,
    save_velocities=True,
    property_map={}
)
# Creates: perturbable0.prm7, perturbable0.rst7, perturbable1.prm7, perturbable1.rst7
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L900-L920)

## Format Conversion

BioSimSpace provides flexible conversion capabilities between different molecular representations through the `Convert` module.

### Generic Conversion Interface

The `to()` function provides a unified interface for all format conversions:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Convert BioSimSpace to Sire
sire_system = BSS.Convert.to(system, "sire")

# Convert BioSimSpace to RDKit
rdkit_mols = BSS.Convert.to(system, "rdkit")

# Convert RDKit to BioSimSpace
bss_system = BSS.Convert.to(rdkit_mols, "biosimspace")

# Chain conversions
bss_system = BSS.Convert.to(
    BSS.Convert.to(system, "sire"),
    "biosimspace"
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L100-L200)

### Specialized Conversion Functions

BioSimSpace provides type-specific conversion functions for clarity:

```python
# Convert to BioSimSpace format
bss_obj = BSS.Convert.toBioSimSpace(sire_object)

# Convert to Sire format
sire_obj = BSS.Convert.toSire(bss_object)

# Convert to RDKit format
rdkit_obj = BSS.Convert.toRDKit(bss_object, force_stereo_inference=False)

# Convert to OpenMM format (platform-dependent)
openmm_obj = BSS.Convert.toOpenMM(bss_object)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L450-L550)

### Conversion Flowchart

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[BioSimSpace Objects] -->|toBioSimSpace| A
    A -->|toSire| B[Sire Objects]
    A -->|toRDKit| C[RDKit Objects]
    A -->|toOpenMM| D[OpenMM Objects]
    
    B -->|toBioSimSpace| A
    C -->|toBioSimSpace| A
    
    subgraph "Hierarchical Conversions"
        E[System] --> F[Molecules]
        F --> G[Molecule]
        G --> H[Residue]
        H --> I[Atom]
    end
    
    style A fill:#bbf,stroke:#333
    style B fill:#bfb,stroke:#333
    style C fill:#fbb,stroke:#333
    style D fill:#fbf,stroke:#333
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L200-L400)

### Stereochemistry Preservation

BioSimSpace preserves stereochemical information during format conversions, with special handling for SDF files:

```python
# Load molecule with stereochemistry
mol = BSS.IO.readMolecules("ligand.sdf")[0]

# Convert to RDKit - stereochemistry is preserved
rdkit_mol = BSS.Convert.toRDKit(mol)

# Force stereochemistry inference if needed
rdkit_mol = BSS.Convert.toRDKit(mol, force_stereo_inference=True)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L450-L500), [tests/Convert/test_convert.py](tests/Convert/test_convert.py#L91-L122)

### SMILES to Molecule Conversion

Generate molecular structures directly from SMILES strings:

```python
# Create molecule from SMILES
mol = BSS.Convert.smiles("CCO")

# With explicit hydrogens
mol = BSS.Convert.smiles("CCO", add_hydrogens=True)

# With coordinates and hydrogens
mol = BSS.Convert.smiles("CCO", generate_coordinates=True)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L70-L100)

### SMILES Special Handling for GROMACS

Molecules generated from SMILES strings starting with `[` characters are automatically renamed to ensure GROMACS compatibility:

```python
# SMILES with special characters
mol = BSS.Convert.smiles("[C@@H](C(F)(F)F)(OC(F)F)Cl")

# Name is automatically prefixed
assert mol._sire_object.name().value() == "smiles:[C@@H](C(F)(F)F)(OC(F)F)Cl"
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L70-L100), [tests/Convert/test_convert.py](tests/Convert/test_convert.py#L77-L89)

## Workflow Integration

### Gateway Node Pattern

BioSimSpace's Gateway module enables creating reusable workflow components for file format conversion:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Create a conversion node
node = BSS.Gateway.Node("A node to convert between molecular file formats")

# Define inputs
node.addInput("files", BSS.Gateway.FileSet(help="A set of molecular input files."))
node.addInput(
    "format",
    BSS.Gateway.String(
        help="The molecular file format to convert to.",
        allowed=BSS.IO.fileFormats(),
        default="PDB",
    ),
)

# Define output
node.addOutput("converted", BSS.Gateway.File(help="The converted molecular system."))

# Process conversion
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(node.getInput("files"))
file_format = node.getInput("format")
node.setOutput("converted", BSS.IO.saveMolecules("converted", system, file_format)[0])
```

Sources: [demo/conversion.py](demo/conversion.py#L24-L104), [demo/conversion.ipynb](demo/conversion.ipynb#L1-L200)

### Conversion Workflow Flowchart

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Input Files] --> B[readMolecules]
    B --> C[BioSimSpace System]
    C --> D{Format Check}
    D -->|Supported| E[saveMolecules]
    D -->|Unsupported| F[raise Error]
    E --> G[Output Files]
    
    H[SMILES String] --> I[Convert.smiles]
    I --> C
    
    J[Other Format] --> K[Convert.to]
    K --> C
```

Sources: [demo/conversion.py](demo/conversion.py#L24-L104)

## Error Handling and Limitations

### Unsupported Features

Certain file format features are not currently supported:

- **CMAP records** in AMBER topology files cause parsing errors
- **CHAMBER files** (AMBER CHARMM force field) are not supported
- **Geometric combining rules** information is lost when writing to AMBER format
- **GROMACS topology** requires GROMACS installation

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L460-L480)

### Common Error Scenarios

```python
try:
    # Missing topology file
    system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["coordinates.rst7"])
except IOError as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")  # "Failed to read molecules... topology file"

try:
    # Unsupported format
    BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, "unsupported_format")
except ValueError as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")  # "Unsupported file format..."

try:
    # OpenMM conversion without OpenMM installed
    openmm_obj = BSS.Convert.toOpenMM(system)
except BSS._Exceptions.ConversionError as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")  # "Conversion to OpenMM format is currently not supported"
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L460-L500), [python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py](python/BioSimSpace/Convert/_convert.py#L250-L280)

## Performance Optimization

### File Caching

BioSimSpace provides optional file caching to optimize repeated I/O operations:

```python
# Enable caching
BSS.IO.enableCache()

# Read files - first read is slow, subsequent reads use cache
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["large_file.prm7", "large_file.rst7"])

# Write files - cached files are copied when identical
BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, "pdb")

# Disable caching
BSS.IO.disableCache()

# Clear cache
BSS.IO.clearCache()
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/__init__.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/__init__.py#L1-L50)

### Batch Processing

Process multiple files efficiently using wildcards:

```python
import glob

# Read all files in a directory
all_files = glob.glob("systems/*.prm7") + glob.glob("systems/*.rst7")

# Process in batch
for i, (top, crd) in enumerate(zip(all_files[::2], all_files[1::2])):
    system = BSS.IO.readMolecules([top, crd])
    BSS.IO.saveMolecules(f"converted_{i}", system, "gro87")
```

## Best Practices

### File Organization

Organize related files together and use descriptive basenames:

```python
# Good: Related files together
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["protein.prm7", "protein.rst7"])
BSS.IO.saveMolecules("protein_gromacs", system, ["gro87", "grotop"])

# Avoid: Unrelated files in same read
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["protein.prm7", "ligand.rst7"])  # May cause errors
```

### Format Selection

Choose appropriate formats for different tasks:

| Task | Recommended Format | Reason |
|------|-------------------|--------|
| Visualization | PDB, SDF | Widely supported, easy to view |
| MD Simulations | AMBER, GROMACS | Complete topology information |
| Exchange | PDB, SDF | Portable, lossless for coordinates |
| Free Energy | AMBER (dual-end state) | Well-supported perturbation protocols |

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L800-L900)

### Property Mapping Consistency

Maintain consistent property mappings across read/write operations:

```python
# Define property mapping once
property_map = {"charge": "my-charge", "forcefield": "ff"}

# Use consistently
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(files, property_map=property_map)
BSS.IO.saveMolecules(output, system, format, property_map=property_map)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L318-L400), [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L600-L800)

## Testing and Validation

BioSimSpace includes comprehensive tests for format handling:

```python
# Test system conversions (from test suite)
def test_system(system):
    sire_system = BSS.Convert.toSire(system)
    rdmols = BSS.Convert.toRDKit(sire_system)
    bss_system = BSS.Convert.toBioSimSpace(rdmols).toSystem()
    
    assert bss_system.nMolecules() == system.nMolecules()
    assert bss_system.nAtoms() == system.nAtoms()
```

Sources: [tests/Convert/test_convert.py](tests/Convert/test_convert.py#L8-L44)

# Working with Molecular Systems



This guide introduces BioSimSpace's molecular system architecture, showing you how to load, manipulate, and query molecular structures for computational workflows. BioSimSpace provides a unified interface for working with molecular systems across multiple simulation engines and file formats, making it ideal for interoperable biomolecular simulations.

## Understanding BioSimSpace's Molecular Architecture

BioSimSpace uses a hierarchical object model to represent molecular systems, with three primary container classes that map to Sire's underlying molecular framework. The System class serves as the top-level container that manages collections of molecules, while Molecule and Molecules represent individual molecules and immutable molecule groups respectively. This design enables intuitive manipulation of complex biomolecular assemblies while maintaining the flexibility needed for simulation workflows.

![Molecular System Architecture](https://github.com/OpenBioSim/biosimspace/blob/devel/paper/figures/fig1.png?raw=true)

The architecture supports operator overloading for intuitive system composition—you can add systems together, subtract molecules, and iterate over molecules naturally. This Pythonic approach makes complex molecular manipulations straightforward and readable.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class System {
        +System(system)
        +addMolecules(molecules)
        +removeMolecules(molecules)
        +getMolecule(index)
        +getMolecules(group)
        +search(query)
        +getCoordinates()
        +setCoordinates(coords)
        +nMolecules()
        +nAtoms()
        +nResidues()
    }
    
    class Molecule {
        +Molecule(molecule)
        +coordinates()
        +getAtoms()
        +getResidues()
        +search(query)
        +copy()
        +nAtoms()
        +nResidues()
        +isPerturbable()
    }
    
    class Molecules {
        +Molecules(molecules)
        +getMolecule(index)
        +toSystem()
        +nMolecules()
    }
    
    System *-- Molecule : contains
    System *-- Molecules : contains
    Molecules o-- Molecule : immutable collection
```

## Reading Molecular Systems from Files

BioSimSpace provides flexible file I/O through the `BioSimSpace.IO` module, supporting over 20 molecular file formats including PDB, AMBER (PRM7/RST7), GROMACS (GROTOP/GRO87), and CHARMM formats. The `readMolecules` function automatically detects file format and handles both local files and remote URLs, making it easy to work with molecular data from various sources.

**Basic Reading Operations:**

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Read from a single file
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules("protein.pdb")

# Read from multiple files (e.g., topology + coordinates)
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["ala.prm7", "ala.rst7"])

# Read from a URL with automatic download
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules("https://files.rcsb.org/download/1a3n.pdb")
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L229-L399)

**Advanced Reading Options:**

The `readMolecules` function accepts several parameters to control system loading behavior:

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `make_whole` | bool | Unwrap molecules split across periodic boundaries | False |
| `rotate_box` | bool | Align box vectors for MD engine compatibility | False |
| `reduce_box` | bool | Reduce box vectors to minimal representation | False |
| `show_warnings` | bool | Display parsing warnings | False |
| `property_map` | dict | Map system properties to custom names | {} |

```python
# Read molecules and make them whole across periodic boundaries
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["complex.prm7", "complex.rst7"], 
                              make_whole=True)

# Rotate box vectors for engine compatibility
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["protein.grotop", "protein.gro87"],
                              rotate_box=True)

# Use custom property mapping
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["system.prm7", "system.rst7"],
                              property_map={"charge": "my-charge"})
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L229-L399)

**Reading from PDB Database:**

BioSimSpace offers convenience methods for working with Protein Data Bank entries. The `readPDB` function can fetch PDB records by ID or process local PDB files with `pdb4amber` for AMBER compatibility.

```python
# Fetch directly from RCSB PDB
system = BSS.IO.readPDB("1a3n")

# Process with pdb4amber for AMBER compatibility
system = BSS.IO.readPDB("protein.pdb", pdb4amber=True)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L104-L266)

## Navigating and Querying Molecular Systems

Once loaded, molecular systems can be navigated using Python's natural indexing and iteration syntax. The System class implements sequence-like behavior, enabling direct access to individual molecules and iteration over the entire system.

**Basic Navigation:**

```python
# Access individual molecules by index
first_molecule = system[0]
last_molecule = system[-1]

# Iterate over all molecules
for molecule in system:
    print(f"Molecule has {molecule.nAtoms()} atoms")

# Slice to get a subset
molecules_5_10 = system[5:10]

# Check system size
n_molecules = len(system)  # or system.nMolecules()
n_atoms = system.nAtoms()
n_residues = system.nResidues()
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L195-L262)

**Powerful Search Capabilities:**

BioSimSpace provides a flexible search syntax for locating atoms, residues, and molecules within systems. The search language supports logical operators, property matching, and case-insensitive patterns.

```python
# Search for residues by name
ala_residues = system.search("resname ALA")

# Case-insensitive search
gly_residues = system.search("resname /gly/i")

# Combine search criteria
carbon_in_ala = system.search("resname ALA and atomname C")

# Search by element
oxygens = system.search("element oxygen")
or_hydrogens = system.search("element oxygen or element hydrogen")

# Search specific indices
specific_atom = system.search("molidx 10 and atomidx 23")

# Get water molecules
water_molecules = system.getWaterMolecules()
n_water = system.nWaterMolecules()

# Get perturbable molecules (for free energy)
perturbable = system.getPerturbableMolecules()
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L1562-L1649)

**Querying System Properties:**

System objects expose various properties through accessor methods, making it easy to inspect system composition and characteristics.

```python
# System composition
print(f"System contains {system.nMolecules()} molecules")
print(f"Total atoms: {system.nAtoms()}")
print(f"Total residues: {system.nResidues()}")

# Charge information
total_charge = system.charge()

# Check for amino acids and nucleotides
n_aa = system.nAminoAcids()
n_nucl = system.nNucleotides()
amino_acids = system.getAminoAcids()

# Check file format if loaded from file
if system.fileFormat():
    print(f"Loaded from {system.fileFormat()} format")
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L302-L400)

## Manipulating Molecular Systems

BioSimSpace provides rich capabilities for manipulating molecular systems, from combining multiple systems to extracting subsets and performing coordinate transformations. These operations are essential for simulation preparation and analysis workflows.

**System Composition:**

```python
# Combine two systems using addition operator
combined_system = system1 + system2

# Create a new system containing only specific molecules
selected = system.getMolecules(group="water")  # Get water molecules
system_without_water = system - selected

# Add molecules to existing system
new_system = system.copy()
new_system.addMolecules(selected)

# Remove molecules from system
system_without_ions = system.removeMolecules(system.search("resname Na+ Cl-"))
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L153-L180)

**Molecule Extraction and Management:**

```python
# Extract individual molecules for processing
molecule = system[0]

# Get specific molecule groups
proteins = system.getMolecules(group="protein")
ligands = system.getMolecules(group="ligand")

# Extract atoms and residues
all_atoms = system.getAtoms()
specific_residue = system.getResidue(5)
all_residues = system.getResidues()

# Convert molecule to system
molecule_system = molecule.toSystem()
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L953-L1074)

> [!TIP]
> When extracting molecules from a system for individual manipulation, use the `.copy()` method to create independent copies. This prevents accidental modifications to the original system. Similarly, system indexing returns a new Molecule object, not a reference into the original system.

**Coordinate Manipulations:**

```python
# Get coordinates
coordinates = system.getCoordinates()

# Set coordinates (useful for applying transformations)
system.setCoordinates(new_coordinates)

# Translate the entire system
from BioSimSpace.Types import Length
translation = [5 * Length.angstrom, 0, 0]
system.translate(translation)

# Translate a single molecule
molecule.translate(translation)

# Make molecules whole across periodic boundaries
system.makeWhole()

# Repartition hydrogen mass (for time step acceleration)
system.repartitionHydrogenMass(factor=4)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L1182-L1969)

## Writing Molecular Systems to Files

Saving molecular systems in various formats enables interoperability with different simulation tools and analysis pipelines. The `saveMolecules` function writes systems to specified formats with options for controlling output properties.

**Basic Writing Operations:**

```python
# Save to AMBER format
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, ["prm7", "rst7"])

# Save to GROMACS format
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("system", system, ["grotop", "gro87"])

# Save to PDB format
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("structure", system, "pdb")

# Save to multiple formats
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, ["pdb", "prm7", "rst7"])
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L527-L820)

**Advanced Writing Options:**

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `match_water` | bool | Update water molecule naming for target format | True |
| `save_velocities` | bool | Include velocity information in output | False |
| `property_map` | dict | Map system properties for output | {} |

```python
# Save without velocities (reduces file size)
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("output", system, "pdb", save_velocities=False)

# Save with custom property mapping
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("system", system, ["grotop", "gro87"],
                            property_map={"charge": "my-charge"})

# Convert between formats with water model matching
files = BSS.IO.saveMolecules("converted", system, ["prm7", "rst7"],
                            match_water=True)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L527-L820)

**Supported File Formats:**

BioSimSpace supports reading and writing to numerous molecular file formats:

| Format | Description | Extensions | Use Case |
|--------|-------------|------------|----------|
| PDB | Protein Data Bank | .pdb | Visualization, sharing |
| PRM7/RST7 | AMBER topology/coords | .prm7, .rst7 | AMBER simulations |
| GROTOP/GRO87 | GROMACS topology/coords | .top, .gro | GROMACS simulations |
| PSF | CHARMM topology | .psf | CHARMM simulations |
| MOL2 | Tripos Mol2 | .mol2 | Small molecule exchange |
| SDF | Structure Data Format | .sdf | Chemical databases |

You can query all available formats programmatically:

```python
# List all supported formats
formats = BSS.IO.fileFormats()

# Get information about a specific format
info = BSS.IO.formatInfo("PDB")
print(info)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L94-L138)

## Working with Perturbable Systems

BioSimSpace has specialized support for perturbable molecular systems used in free energy calculations. These systems contain two endpoint states (lambda = 0 and lambda = 1) representing different molecular configurations.

**Identifying Perturbable Systems:**

```python
# Check if system contains perturbable molecules
n_perturbable = system.nPerturbableMolecules()

if n_perturbable > 0:
    perturbable_molecules = system.getPerturbableMolecules()
    print(f"System has {n_perturbable} perturbable molecule(s)")
    
    # Check if individual molecule is perturbable
    for mol in perturbable_molecules:
        if mol.isPerturbable():
            print(f"Molecule {mol.number()} is perturbable")
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py](python/BioSimSpace/_SireWrappers/_system.py#L1151-L1195)

**Reading and Writing Perturbable Systems:**

```python
# Read a perturbable system from file
perturbable_system = BSS.IO.readPerturbableSystem(
    "morph.pert", 
    "ligand.prm7", 
    "ligand.rst7",
    "protein.prm7",
    "protein.rst7"
)

# Save a perturbable system
files = BSS.IO.savePerturbableSystem(
    "output",
    perturbable_system,
    ["prm7", "rst7"]
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py](python/BioSimSpace/IO/_io.py#L38-L40)

## Practical Workflow Example

Here's a complete example demonstrating common molecular system operations for simulation preparation:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# 1. Read a protein-ligand complex
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["complex.prm7", "complex.rst7"])

# 2. Analyze the system
print(f"Loaded system with {system.nMolecules()} molecules")
print(f"Total atoms: {system.nAtoms()}")
print(f"Total charge: {system.charge()}")

# 3. Separate protein and ligand
proteins = system.getMolecules(group="protein")
ligands = system.getMolecules(group="ligand")
waters = system.getMolecules(group="water")
ions = system.getMolecules(group="ion")

print(f"Protein: {len(proteins)} molecules, {proteins.nAtoms()} atoms")
print(f"Ligand: {len(ligands)} molecules, {ligands.nAtoms()} atoms")
print(f"Water: {waters.nMolecules()} molecules")
print(f"Ions: {ions.nMolecules()} molecules")

# 4. Extract and prepare ligand for separate analysis
ligand = ligands[0]
ligand_coords = ligand.coordinates()

# 5. Search for specific residues
active_site = system.search("resname HIS and (resid 57 or resid 102)")
print(f"Found {len(active_site)} active site histidines")

# 6. Create a system without water for minimization
solvent = waters + ions
dry_system = system - solvent

# 7. Save in different formats
BSS.IO.saveMolecules("protein_ligand", system, ["prm7", "rst7"])
BSS.IO.saveMolecules("protein_ligand", system, "pdb")
BSS.IO.saveMolecules("dry_complex", dry_system, "pdb")
```

Sources: [demo/molecular_setup.py](demo/molecular_setup.py#L1-L150)

## Best Practices and Common Patterns

**Error Handling:**

Always validate system contents before operations:

```python
# Check if system contains expected components
if system.nMolecules() == 0:
    raise ValueError("System is empty")

# Verify molecule extraction succeeded
if len(ligands) == 0:
    raise ValueError("No ligands found in system")

# Use try-except for search operations
try:
    results = system.search("invalid query")
except ValueError as e:
    print(f"Search failed: {e}")
```

**Memory Management:**

For large systems, work with subsets rather than keeping full copies:

```python
# Work with specific molecules rather than copying entire system
for i in range(min(10, system.nMolecules())):
    mol = system[i]
    # Process molecule without copying system
    
# Use Molecules container for immutable groups
subset = system.getMolecules(group="protein")
```

> [!TIP]
> When working with periodic systems, use `make_whole=True` when reading if you need intact molecules for analysis. This is particularly important for ligands that may cross periodic boundaries. For simulation setup, you may want to keep molecules split to maintain periodic boundary conditions.

# MD Protocols Overview



BioSimSpace provides a comprehensive protocol system for configuring molecular dynamics simulations. Protocols encapsulate all simulation parameters—runtime, temperature, pressure, time steps, restraints, and sampling methods—into reusable, interoperable objects that work across different MD backends. This abstraction enables the same protocol definition to execute with AMBER, GROMACS, NAMD, OpenMM, or SOMD without modification.

## Protocol Architecture

BioSimSpace's protocol system is built on a foundation of composable mixins and specialized protocol classes that inherit from a common base. This design enables code reuse through shared functionality while maintaining clean separation of concerns for different simulation types.

The base `Protocol` class [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_protocol.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_protocol.py#L30-L31) provides the foundation, with specialized protocols extending this base and incorporating mixins for common features like position restraints and free energy calculations. The protocol system automatically discovers and registers available protocols through reflection in the utility module.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Protocol {
        <<abstract>>
        +getRestraint()
        +_setCustomised()
    }
    
    class _PositionRestraintMixin {
        +restraint: str|list
        +force_constant: GeneralUnit
        +getRestraint()
        +setRestraint()
        +getForceConstant()
        +setForceConstant()
        +restraints(): list
    }
    
    class _FreeEnergyMixin {
        +lam: float
        +lam_vals: list
        +min_lam: float
        +max_lam: float
        +num_lam: int
        +perturbation_type: str
        +getPerturbationType()
        +setPerturbationType()
        +getLambda()
        +getLambdaIndex()
        +getLambdaValues()
        +setLambdaValues()
    }
    
    Protocol <|-- Minimisation
    Protocol <|-- Equilibration
    Protocol <|-- Production
    Protocol <|-- FreeEnergyMinimisation
    Protocol <|-- FreeEnergyEquilibration
    Protocol <|-- FreeEnergyProduction
    Protocol <|-- Metadynamics
    Protocol <|-- Steering
    Protocol <|-- Custom
    
    _PositionRestraintMixin <-- Minimisation
    _PositionRestraintMixin <-- Equilibration
    _PositionRestraintMixin <-- Production
    _FreeEnergyMixin <-- FreeEnergyMinimisation
    _FreeEnergyMixin <-- FreeEnergyEquilibration
    _FreeEnergyMixin <-- FreeEnergyProduction
    
    class Minimisation {
        +steps: int
        +getSteps()
        +setSteps()
    }
    
    class Equilibration {
        +timestep: Time
        +runtime: Time
        +temperature_start: Temperature
        +temperature_end: Temperature
        +pressure: Pressure
        +thermostat_time_constant: Time
        +report_interval: int
        +restart_interval: int
        +restart: bool
        +isConstantTemp()
    }
    
    class Production {
        +timestep: Time
        +runtime: Time
        +temperature: Temperature
        +pressure: Pressure
        +thermostat_time_constant: Time
        +report_interval: int
        +restart_interval: int
        +restart: bool
    }
    
    class Metadynamics {
        +collective_variable: CollectiveVariable
        +hill_height: Energy
        +hill_frequency: int

        +setCollectiveVariable()
```

## Standard MD Protocols

BioSimSpace provides three core protocols that form the backbone of most molecular dynamics workflows: minimization, equilibration, and production simulations. Each protocol is designed for a specific stage of the simulation workflow and offers appropriate default parameters.

### Minimisation Protocol

The `Minimisation` protocol performs energy minimization to relieve bad contacts and steric clashes in the initial molecular system. This is typically the first step in any simulation workflow.

**Key Parameters:**
- `steps` (int, default: 10000): Maximum number of minimization steps
- `restraint` (str or list, default: None): Type of position restraint
- `force_constant` (GeneralUnit, default: 10 kcal/mol/Å²): Restraint force constant

**Restraint Options:**
- `"backbone"`: Protein backbone atoms (matched by name template)
- `"heavy"`: All non-hydrogen atoms excluding water and ions
- `"all"`: All atoms excluding water and ions
- List of integers: Custom atom indices for fine-grained control

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Default minimisation protocol
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Minimisation()
print(protocol)  # <BioSimSpace.Protocol.Minimisation: steps=10000, restraint=None>

# Custom minimisation with backbone restraints
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Minimisation(
    steps=5000,
    restraint="backbone",
    force_constant=100 * BSS.Units.Energy.kj_per_mol / BSS.Units.Length.nanometer**2
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py#L37-L38), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py#L40-L60)

### Equilibration Protocol

The `Equilibration` protocol brings the system to equilibrium at target temperature and optionally pressure. It supports heating/cooling protocols and includes position restraints for stable equilibration.

**Key Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `timestep` | Time | 2 fs | Integration time step |
| `runtime` | Time | 1 ns | Total simulation runtime |
| `temperature_start` | Temperature | 300 K | Starting temperature |
| `temperature_end` | Temperature | 300 K | Target temperature |
| `pressure` | Pressure | None | Target pressure (None = NVT ensemble) |
| `thermostat_time_constant` | Time | 1 ps | Thermostat coupling constant |
| `report_interval` | int | 200 | Steps between coordinate reports |
| `restart_interval` | int | 1000 | Steps between checkpoint files |
| `restart` | bool | False | Restart from previous simulation |
| `restraint` | str/list | None | Position restraint type |
| `force_constant` | GeneralUnit | 10 kcal/mol/Å² | Restraint force constant |

**Usage Example:**
```python
# Heating protocol from 0 to 300 K with backbone restraints
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    runtime=0.05 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature_start=0 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    temperature_end=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere,
    restraint="backbone"
)

# Constant temperature equilibration
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_equilibration.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_equilibration.py#L37-L38), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_equilibration.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_equilibration.py#L40-L54)

### Production Protocol

The `Production` protocol runs production molecular dynamics simulations at constant temperature and pressure (NPT ensemble) or constant temperature (NVT ensemble if pressure is None). This is the final stage where data is collected for analysis.

**Key Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `timestep` | Time | 2 fs | Integration time step |
| `runtime` | Time | 1 ns | Total simulation runtime |
| `temperature` | Temperature | 300 K | Simulation temperature |
| `pressure` | Pressure | 1 atm | Simulation pressure |
| `thermostat_time_constant` | Time | 1 ps | Thermostat coupling constant |
| `report_interval` | int | 200 | Steps between coordinate reports |
| `restart_interval` | int | 1000 | Steps between checkpoint files |
| `restart` | bool | False | Restart from previous simulation |
| `restraint` | str/list | None | Position restraint type |
| `force_constant` | GeneralUnit | 10 kcal/mol/Å² | Restraint force constant |

**Usage Example:**
```python
# Standard NPT production run
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    runtime=5 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere
)

# Longer production with increased reporting
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    runtime=20 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=298 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere,
    report_interval=100,
    restart_interval=500
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_production.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_production.py#L37-L38), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_production.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_production.py#L40-L52)

## Free Energy Protocols

BioSimSpace provides specialized protocols for alchemical free energy calculations using thermodynamic perturbation methods. These protocols extend the standard MD protocols with lambda state scheduling and perturbation configuration.

### Free Energy Protocol Variants

The free energy protocol family includes three variants that mirror the standard MD workflow:

1. **FreeEnergyMinimisation**: Minimization at a specific lambda state
2. **FreeEnergyEquilibration**: Equilibration at a specific lambda state
3. **FreeEnergyProduction** (aliased as `FreeEnergy`): Production sampling across lambda windows

### Lambda Configuration

Free energy protocols include lambda scheduling parameters controlled by the `_FreeEnergyMixin`:

**Key Lambda Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `lam` | float | 0.0 | Current lambda value (for single state) |
| `lam_vals` | list | None | Explicit list of lambda values |
| `min_lam` | float | 0.0 | Minimum lambda value |
| `max_lam` | float | 1.0 | Maximum lambda value |
| `num_lam` | int | 11 | Number of lambda windows |
| `perturbation_type` | str | "full" | Type of perturbation |

**Perturbation Types:**
- `"full"`: Full perturbation (both A→B and B→A)
- `"forward"`: Forward perturbation only
- `"reverse"`: Reverse perturbation only

**Usage Example:**
```python
# Free energy production with custom lambda schedule
protocol = BSS.Protocol.FreeEnergy(
    timestep=2 * BSS.Units.Time.femtosecond,
    runtime=4 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere,
    min_lam=0.0,
    max_lam=1.0,
    num_lam=11,
    perturbation_type="full"
)

# Get lambda values
print(protocol.getLambdaValues())  # [0.0, 0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0]

# Single-state minimization at lambda=0.5
minimisation = BSS.Protocol.FreeEnergyMinimisation(lam=0.5)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_production.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_production.py#L35-L36), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_mixin.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_mixin.py#L30-L31), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_mixin.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_mixin.py#L33-L41)

## Enhanced Sampling Protocols

BioSimSpace supports advanced sampling techniques through specialized protocols that go beyond standard MD to improve conformational sampling efficiency.

### Metadynamics Protocol

The `Metadynamics` protocol implements well-tempered metadynamics for enhanced sampling along defined collective variables (CVs). This protocol adds Gaussian bias potentials along CVs to escape local minima and explore free energy landscapes.

**Key Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `collective_variable` | CollectiveVariable | Required | CV to bias |
| `timestep` | Time | 2 fs | Integration time step |
| `runtime` | Time | 1 ns | Total simulation runtime |
| `temperature` | Temperature | 300 K | Simulation temperature |
| `pressure` | Pressure | 1 atm | Simulation pressure |
| `thermostat_time_constant` | Time | 1 ps | Thermostat coupling constant |
| `hill_height` | Energy | 1 kJ/mol | Initial Gaussian height |
| `hill_frequency` | int | 1000 | Steps between hill additions |
| `report_interval` | int | 1000 | Steps between coordinate reports |
| `restart_interval` | int | 1000 | Steps between checkpoint files |
| `bias_factor` | float | None | Well-tempered bias factor |

**Usage Example:**
```python
# Define a torsional collective variable
cv = BSS.Metadynamics.CollectiveVariable.Torsion(atoms=[0, 1, 2, 3])

# Well-tempered metadynamics
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Metadynamics(
    collective_variable=cv,
    runtime=5 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    hill_height=1.2 * BSS.Units.Energy.kj_per_mol,
    hill_frequency=500,
    bias_factor=10
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_metadynamics.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_metadynamics.py#L39-L40), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_metadynamics.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_metadynamics.py#L42-L55)

### Steering Protocol

The `Steering` protocol implements steered molecular dynamics (SMD) to drive the system along a defined collective variable trajectory using time-dependent harmonic restraints. This is useful for studying transition pathways and reaction mechanisms.

**Key Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `collective_variable` | CollectiveVariable | Required | CV to steer |
| `schedule` | list[Time] | Required | Timeline of restraint stages |
| `restraints` | list[Restraint] | Required | Restraints at each stage |
| `verse` | str | "both" | Steering direction |
| `timestep` | Time | 2 fs | Integration time step |
| `runtime` | Time | 1 ns | Total simulation runtime |
| `temperature` | Temperature | 300 K | Simulation temperature |
| `pressure` | Pressure | 1 atm | Simulation pressure |
| `thermostat_time_constant` | Time | 1 ps | Thermostat coupling constant |
| `report_interval` | int | 1000 | Steps between coordinate reports |
| `restart_interval` | int | 1000 | Steps between checkpoint files |
| `colvar_file` | str | None | External colvar config file |

**Verse Options:**
- `"both"`: Steer in both directions
- `"forward"`: Steer forward only
- `"reverse"`: Steer reverse only

**Usage Example:**
```python
# Define RMSD collective variable
cv = BSS.Metadynamics.CollectiveVariable.RMSD(system, reference, ...)

# Create steering schedule (time points for each stage)
schedule = [
    0 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,      # Start
    4 * BSS.Units.Time.picosecond,      # Apply force
    150 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,    # Steer
    152 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond     # Relax
]

# Define restraints at each stage
nm = BSS.Units.Length.nanometer
restraints = [
    BSS.Metadynamics.Restraint(cv.getInitialValue(), 0),      # No restraint
    BSS.Metadynamics.Restraint(cv.getInitialValue(), 3500),  # Hold start
    BSS.Metadynamics.Restraint(0 * nm, 3500),                # Steer to target
    BSS.Metadynamics.Restraint(0 * nm, 0)                     # Release
]

# Create steering protocol
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Steering(
    collective_variable=cv,
    schedule=schedule,
    restraints=restraints,
    verse="both",
    runtime=200 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=298 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere
)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_steering.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_steering.py#L39-L40), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_steering.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_steering.py#L42-L56)

## Custom Protocol

The `Custom` protocol allows users to define simulation protocols using custom configuration files (e.g., AMBER's `mdin`, GROMACS's `mdp`, NAMD's configuration). This provides maximum flexibility for users who need to use engine-specific features not exposed through the standard protocol interfaces.

> [!TIP]
> Custom protocols are engine-specific and may not be portable across different MD backends. Use standard protocols whenever possible to maintain workflow interoperability.

**Usage Example:**
```python
# Load a custom AMBER configuration file
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Custom("amber_config.in")

# The protocol can be passed to BSS.MD.run() like any other protocol
process = BSS.MD.run(system, protocol)
```

## Position Restraints

Position restraints are a powerful feature that allow selective immobilization of atoms during simulation. This is particularly useful for equilibration, where restraining the protein backbone while allowing solvent to relax prevents structural drift.

### Restraint Types

The `_PositionRestraintMixin` provides consistent restraint handling across protocols:

| Restraint Type | Description | Use Case |
|----------------|-------------|----------|
| `"backbone"` | Protein backbone atoms (C, N, CA, O) | Protein equilibration |
| `"heavy"` | Non-hydrogen atoms (excluding water/ions) | Solvent relaxation |
| `"all"` | All atoms (excluding water/ions) | Selective immobilization |
| List[int] | Custom atom indices | Fine-grained control |
| `None` | No restraints | Free simulation |

### Force Constant Specification

Force constants support both typed `GeneralUnit` objects and string-based unit specification:

```python
# Using typed units
force_constant = 10 * BSS.Units.Energy.kcal_per_mol / BSS.Units.Length.angstrom2

# Using strings (equivalent)
force_constant = "10 kcal / (mol angstrom2)"
force_constant = "100 kJ / (mol nm2)"
```

### Usage Example

```python
# Backbone restraint with default force constant
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    restraint="backbone"
)

# Heavy atom restraint with custom force constant
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    restraint="heavy",
    force_constant=50 * BSS.Units.Energy.kcal_per_mol / BSS.Units.Length.angstrom2
)

# Custom atom indices (e.g., ligand atoms only)
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Minimisation(
    restraint=[100, 101, 102, 103],  # Specific atom indices
    force_constant="100 kJ / (mol nm2)"
)

# Get available restraint types
print(BSS.Protocol.Equilibration.restraints())
# ['backbone', 'heavy', 'all', 'none']
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_position_restraint_mixin.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_position_restraint_mixin.py#L32-L33), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_position_restraint_mixin.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_position_restraint_mixin.py#L35-L36), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py#L51-L60)

## Protocol Creation and Discovery

BioSimSpace provides utility functions for programmatic protocol discovery and creation, particularly useful in workflow nodes and automation scripts.

### Listing Available Protocols

The `protocols()` function returns a list of all available MD protocols:

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Get all supported protocols
protocols = BSS.Protocol.protocols()
print(protocols)
# ['Minimisation', 'Equilibration', 'Production', 'FreeEnergyMinimisation',
#  'FreeEnergyEquilibration', 'FreeEnergy', 'FreeEnergyProduction',
#  'Metadynamics', 'Steering', 'Custom', 'ATMMinimisation', 'ATMEquilibration',
#  'ATMAnnealing', 'ATMProduction']
```

### Dynamic Protocol Creation

The `createProtocol()` factory function creates default protocol instances from string names, enabling user-driven protocol selection in workflows:

```python
# Create protocols dynamically by name
protocol = BSS.Protocol.createProtocol("Minimisation")
protocol = BSS.Protocol.createProtocol("Equilibration")
protocol = BSS.Protocol.createProtocol("Production")

# Case and whitespace insensitive
protocol = BSS.Protocol.createProtocol("minimisation")
protocol = BSS.Protocol.createProtocol("free energy")

# Useful in workflow nodes with user input
user_protocol = node.getInput("protocol_name")  # e.g., "Equilibration"
protocol = BSS.Protocol.createProtocol(user_protocol)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_utils.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_utils.py#L42-L73), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_utils.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_utils.py#L75-L95)

## Unit-Based Parameter Specification

BioSimSpace protocols support flexible parameter specification using either typed `GeneralUnit` objects or human-readable string representations. This dual approach enables both programmatic precision and user-friendly configuration.

### Typed Units

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Using typed units (recommended for scripts)
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    timestep=2 * BSS.Units.Time.femtosecond,
    runtime=5 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=298.15 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere
)
```

### String-Based Units

```python
# Using string-based units (convenient for notebooks/workflows)
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    timestep="2fs",
    runtime="5ns",
    temperature="298.15K",
    pressure="1atm"
)

# Complex unit expressions
protocol = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    force_constant="100 kJ / (mol nm2)",
    thermostat_time_constant="1ps"
)
```

Both approaches produce equivalent protocol objects and can be mixed within the same protocol definition. The string parser supports a wide range of unit expressions and handles pluralization, spacing, and ordering variations.

Sources: [tests/Protocol/test_protocol.py](tests/Protocol/test_protocol.py#L1-L170)

## Protocol Usage in MD Workflows

Protocols are designed to work seamlessly with the `BSS.MD.run()` function, which automatically selects an appropriate MD backend based on the system, protocol, and available hardware.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Load System<br/>BSS.IO.readMolecules] --> B[Create Protocol<br/>BSS.Protocol.X]
    B --> C[Run Simulation<br/>BSS.MD.run]
    C --> D[Monitor Process<br/>Process Management]
    D --> E[Analyze Results<br/>System & Trajectory]
```

**Complete Workflow Example:**

```python
import BioSimSpace as BSS

# Load molecular system
system = BSS.IO.readMolecules(["amber/ala/ala.crd", "amber/ala/ala.top"])

# Create minimisation protocol
min_protocol = BSS.Protocol.Minimisation(steps=10000)
min_process = BSS.MD.run(system, min_protocol)

# Get minimised system
minimised_system = min_process.getSystem(block=True)

# Create equilibration protocol
eq_protocol = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    runtime=0.05 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature_start=0 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    temperature_end=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere,
    restraint="backbone"
)
eq_process = BSS.MD.run(minimised_system, eq_protocol)

# Create production protocol
prod_protocol = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    runtime=2 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    pressure=1 * BSS.Units.Pressure.atmosphere
)
prod_process = BSS.MD.run(eq_process.getSystem(block=True), prod_protocol)

# Get final trajectory
system = prod_process.getSystem(block=True)
trajectory = prod_process.getTrajectory(block=True)
```

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/MD/_md.py](python/BioSimSpace/MD/_md.py#L245-L256), [demo/minimisation.py](demo/minimisation.py#L100-L135), [demo/interactive_md.ipynb](demo/interactive_md.ipynb#L35-L50)

## Protocol Best Practices

### Protocol Chaining

Always chain protocols sequentially, using the output of one as the input to the next. This ensures the system evolves smoothly through the simulation pipeline:

1. **Minimisation** → Relieve bad contacts
2. **Equilibration** → Reach thermodynamic equilibrium
3. **Production** → Collect data for analysis

### Restraint Strategy

Use restraints strategically during equilibration, then release them for production:

```python
# Stage 1: Backbone restrained equilibration
eq1 = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    runtime=0.1 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature_start=0 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    temperature_end=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    restraint="backbone"
)

# Stage 2: Unrestrained equilibration
eq2 = BSS.Protocol.Equilibration(
    runtime=0.1 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin,
    restraint=None  # Release restraints
)

# Stage 3: Production
prod = BSS.Protocol.Production(
    runtime=5 * BSS.Units.Time.nanosecond,
    temperature=300 * BSS.Units.Temperature.kelvin
)
```

### Report and Restart Intervals

Adjust intervals based on simulation length and storage considerations:

| Simulation Length | Report Interval | Restart Interval |
|-------------------|-----------------|------------------|
| < 1 ns | 100-200 | 500-1000 |
| 1-10 ns | 200-500 | 1000-2000 |
| > 10 ns | 500-1000 | 2000-5000 |

> [!TIP]
> Restart intervals should be short enough to minimize data loss if a job fails, but long enough to avoid excessive I/O overhead. A good rule of thumb is one checkpoint every 0.1-0.5 ns of simulation time.

## Protocol Feature Matrix

| Feature | Minimisation | Equilibration | Production | FreeEnergy | Metadynamics | Steering | Custom |
|---------|-------------|---------------|------------|------------|--------------|----------|--------|
| Energy Minimization | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | Depends |
| Temperature Control | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Depends |
| Pressure Control | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Depends |
| Position Restraints | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | Depends |
| Lambda Scheduling | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | Depends |
| Collective Variables | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | Depends |
| Default Runtime | N/A | 1 ns | 1 ns | 4 ns | 1 ns | 1 ns | N/A |
| Default Temperature | N/A | 300 K | 300 K | 300 K | 300 K | 300 K | N/A |
| Default Pressure | N/A | None | 1 atm | 1 atm | 1 atm | 1 atm | N/A |

Sources: [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/__init__.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/__init__.py#L32-L52), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_minimisation.py#L37-L38), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_equilibration.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_equilibration.py#L37-L38), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_production.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_production.py#L37-L38), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_production.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_free_energy_production.py#L35-L36), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_metadynamics.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_metadynamics.py#L39-L40), [python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_steering.py](python/BioSimSpace/Protocol/_steering.py#L39-L40)
